ideas.title: VOA non-domestic rating list (England & Wales business rates) on gankdat: rateable-value lookup + weekly change feed
ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-09 (burn-down starvation fallback), read through the relay (docs/relay/responses/voa-rating-list-2026-10-09, pruned after 7 days). Supply: the Valuation Office (part of HMRC since 2026-04-01) publishes the whole non-domestic rating list and the summary valuations for England and Wales free of charge at voaratinglists.blob.core.windows.net/html/rlidata.htm — epoch snapshots per list year (2026 epoch 0004, 2023 epoch 0023, 2017 and 2010 still maintained), weekly change-update files applied on top of the latest epoch, asterisk-delimited ASCII CSV inside zips of 2M+ rows, a blob-storage directory listing for automation, and a layout PDF (Compiled Rating List and Summary Valuation Data Specification) — exactly the shape of a weekly change feed (new assessments, deletions and rateable-value changes per billing authority) that rating agents, fit-out and energy suppliers and property investors would pay for. Licence, verbatim from the download page: "VO Rating List Downloads are only available under our restricted licence terms and conditions. These are the same terms and conditions applicable to viewing rating list information online. An open government licence does not apply." The terms (tax.service.gov.uk/business-rates-find/terms-and-conditions): "Publication of this information and its use is restricted to Non Domestic Rating (NDR) purposes only" — anyone viewing assessments, and an interested person (occupier or owner), the billing authority, their authorised representative or a firm serving them, reviewing their own and comparable valuations; "Onward disclosure to a third party is prohibited except where the third party's use is for the uses stated above"; the user "will delete this information when they no longer have a business need associated with the stated purposes"; Crown copyright and Crown database right. A gankdat dataset, MCP tool or Apify actor sold to anyone is onward disclosure for a non-NDR purpose — the same category as Land Registry CCOD/OCOD and the FCA register (STRATEGY §5). Demand exists and the one priced rival ignores the licence: Apify spookyweb/uk-business-rates, "from $0.60 / 1,000 valuations", pay-per-event, 2 users total and 1 monthly, no run count shown, resells the same list filtered by postcode, council, description code and value range (WebSearch 2026-10-09; its .md listing returns 404 through the relay). No priced change-alert service for rating surveyors was found; Analyse LOCAL (G-Cloud) sells rating-list analysis to councils on quote; HMRC's Business Rates API is a private trial for registered ratepayers. Declined on licence, not demand.
ideas.trigger: the Valuation Office moves the downloads to the Open Government Licence (the 2023 'transparency and disclosure of information on business rates valuations' consultation points that way) — then relay-read the data specification PDF and RANGE=0-4095 of the latest 2026 change-update zip and score it for the gankdat queue; or a rating agent (an authorised representative under the terms) asks for comparables for its own clients — then a private per-customer feed under their licence, never a shelf listing

ideas.title: UK grants awarded (360Giving / GrantNav aggregate, ~580k grants from ~200 funders) on gankdat: funder and recipient lookup + new-grants change feed, joined to uk-charities by charity number
ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-10 (burn-down starvation pass, WebSearch only — the sandbox resolves no data host, so the file headers are unread). Supply: 360Giving aggregates grants that UK funders publish in its open standard; GrantNav offers the entire dataset as CSV or JSON for download (very large; "store locally"), updated once a day overnight, and GrantNav loads only data published under a licence allowing re-use for any purpose (OGL or CC BY 4.0, attribution to each publisher) — but the licence is set per publisher and a data.gov.uk record describes the GrantNav release as CC BY-SA, so a build must read each publisher's licence field and drop share-alike publishers (a BY-SA row would taint the product). The Datastore (bulk route 360Giving recommends) needs a request form and a code of conduct whose commercial-use terms were not readable from here; GrantNav's own API is explicitly not for building on. Scale from a dated 360Giving post: 583,000 grants worth over £108bn from 196 funders; recipients carry charity and company numbers, so the join to uk-charities / uk-company-profiles is free. Demand: Funds Online (Directory of Social Change) sells funder data at £450–475 + VAT per user per year (8,000 funders, £8bn), with charity tiers to £1,416 — the paying buyer is fundraisers and bid writers wanting "who funded organisations like mine, how much, when"; no Apify actor covers 360Giving or UK charitable grants (the nearest, parseforge/ukri-gateway-to-research-scraper, is research grants), so the shelf has no rival at all. Blind Mode: individual recipients (the standard allows them) dropped whole, organisation recipients kept; grant titles/descriptions kept. Score ≈ 3: evidence 3 (a priced incumbent at £450/yr, an empty Apify shelf, but no inbound ask and the licence per publisher unverified) × reach 2 (Apify, MCP, x402, the /stats funder pages) ÷ 2 build days (daily bulk file → D1 with idOf on the grant identifier, licence filter, per-funder facets, actor + landing card) — above the ICO and Land Registry parks, still behind the distribution items STRATEGY §5 puts first. Parked, not promoted: every data shelf sits at the 2-user floor (exchange 2026-W41) and the share-alike question decides whether the dataset can exist.

ideas.title: Permissionless keeper work on Base: calling public protocol functions that pay the caller a small reward (liquidations with a bonus, harvests, rebalances, oracle pokes) from the existing wallet, gas-limited to a £10 budget
ideas.why: Owner idea 2026-10-11. Many DeFi protocols pay whoever triggers maintenance — by design, so it is allowed. The money is small and flows constantly; the competition on L2s is thinner than on mainnet. Not trading (no position, no price view): ARCHITECTURE's trading rejection does not cover it, but the ledger rule does — a gas budget of £10 at most, simulated before any spend, stop on the first unprofitable week. Primary sources: the protocols' own docs and contracts (Aave v3, Morpho, Compound v3 on Base), Base gas prices, a simulation over recent blocks. — Exchange 2026-W42 (0.6): the simulation the trigger asked for could not run — the sandbox blocks every RPC and explorer, the relay is GET-only (JSON-RPC is POST), Blockscout's Base API answered 403 to the runner and Routescan does not carry Base — so no number this week. Noted for the read: Aave v3 Base liquidation bonuses are 5–7.5% (governance proposal 299, cbBTC onboarding), so a winning liquidation is net positive after Base gas by construction; the question is contention — whether anything is left for a keeper polling once a minute from a Worker cron. — Spike 2026-10-17 (docs/exchange/spikes/keeper-rewards.md), 7 days of Base liquidations read on-chain through the relay: Aave v3 37 events, US$6,523 of bonus, 93 % to one address, median event US$0.66; Morpho Blue 620 events, US$153,005 of incentive, 85 % to five of 48 callers, 97 % of events on two crash days, the 43 long-tail callers earned a median US$18.72 for the week; gas median US$0.08–0.17 a transaction, so £10 buys 77–158 attempts — gas is not the constraint, repayment capital (median Morpho event repays ≈ US$49; the wallet holds US$1.11) or a flash-liquidation contract, a sub-block cadence and a paid RPC are. Liquidation keeping declined; the idea stays parked for the one capital-free shape (harvest call fees). — Research 2026-10-19 (burn-down): the harvest-fee trigger is now `spike-beefy-harvest-call-fees` in new-ventures — Beefy's docs charge fees on every harvest() to the caller, strategist and treasury; the caller's share is quoted at 0.5 % of harvest rewards on mainnet (third-party mirror); Base figure and a week of StratHarvest logs are the spike. — Spike 2026-10-19 (docs/exchange/spikes/beefy-harvest-call-fees.md): declined outright per the trigger — Beefy's fee configuration pays the harvest caller 0.01 % of yield on every Base vault, the chain's 226 active vaults (US$14.98 M TVL, ≈ US$52k weekly yield) cap the entire call-fee pool at US$5.20 a week, and a 6.7-hour log sample shows one bot taking 89 % of 477 harvests (≈ US$0.59 a week left for ten other addresses, below gas). Liquidations (10-17) and harvests (10-19) both measured; no permissionless-reward line pays on Base.

ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-11 (burn-down, WebSearch of the primary docs): the Bazaar is the catalogue agents query for x402-paid services (CDP `discover-services`, `list-bazaar-resources` MCP tool). Listing is automatic — no form, no fee: a seller behind the CDP facilitator (ours, live on Base) configures discovery metadata on each route (explicit `GET /x402/data/<slug>`, description, mimeType, input schema; `validate-endpoint` dry-runs it without paying) and the first successful settled call indexes the resource (docs.cdp.coinbase.com/x402/seller/get-discovered, /x402/bazaar). Size: ~16k resources in the catalogue in September (cdp-sdk issue #806, a seller's pull of 15,874), 34,062 listings on 2,158 hosts in a third-party 2026-10-09 snapshot of which 44.7% are templated bulk hosts — so ~18k real listings and no UK government-register seller found by name. Demand: x402 on Base passed 100M transactions in three quarters (Chainalysis); Artemis/Visa count ~109.6M transactions and ~US$15M filtered volume to 2026-04-21, headline counters are stale or leaderboard-inflated (Coinbase: 25–30% may be leaderboard farming). Our side: `/x402/data/<slug>` is live at US$0.005–0.01 a call with 0 payments ever; the routes are keyed by path only with no description or schema, so nothing could be indexed even after a sale; tonight the preview wall names x402 first (gankdat `preview-wall-next-steps`), which is the one place a keyless agent learns the endpoint exists. Build ≈ 0.2 d (route config + a `validate-endpoint` probe through the relay; add docs.cdp.coinbase.com to the relay hosts), £0; indexing needs one real paid call, which the sandbox never makes (a self-paid half-cent is still money and a leaderboard-shaped signal). Not a paid-rival market: the shelf is the channel; the rivals are the other ~18k listings. Risk: sellers report resources passing validation yet never indexed (issues #806, #759) — the proof must be read from `list-bazaar-resources`, not assumed. — Exchange 2026-W42 winner (13.7 raw, 9 applied): the discovery API read on 2026-10-14 shows 34,668 resources, 518,867 paid calls and 17,160 payer-slots across the top 200 in 30 days, every indexed resource on x402 v2 and no UK register in the catalogue; queued in gankdat.json with the v2 lane upgrade, a merchant reading and a day-30 read (docs/exchange/2026-W42.md).

ideas.title: EPC register (England & Wales Energy Performance Certificates, MHCLG bulk data + API) on gankdat: rating lookup by UPRN/postcode and a D–G-rated lead feed for retrofit installers and letting agents
ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-12 (burn-down starvation fallback), read through the relay (docs/relay/responses/epc-terms-{,2-,3-}2026-10-12, pruned after 7 days). Supply: epc.opendatacommunities.org now redirects to the GOV.UK beta service get-energy-performance-data.communities.gov.uk — bulk CSV downloads and OpenAPI 3 developer APIs for domestic EPCs, non-domestic EPCs and DECs, certificates since 2012, England and Wales only; both need a GOV.UK One Login account (owner identity) for a bearer token. Licence, verbatim from /guidance/licensing-restrictions: "All data fields other than the address and postcode data (address, address 1, address 2, address 3, postcode) available via this website are licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0, which includes Ordnance Survey UPRNs"; the address fields carry an Ordnance Survey and Royal Mail copyright and database-right notice that permits their use "solely for specific purposes related to the energy performance of buildings" — property management for energy efficiency, research, "Promoting and marketing energy efficiency improvements that may be made through a government energy efficiency programme or initiative", the sale/rental market, enforcement — and "Any use of address data which is not specified in this notice … requires an appropriate licence from Ordnance Survey"; anyone sharing address data "must include a copy of this copyright and database right notice with the data". /guidance/data-protection-requirements: "Address level data concerning the energy performance of buildings constitute personal data" — a re-user "will become a data controller", MHCLG keeps the registrant's email, and the page names "unwanted direct marketing" as the misuse to report to the ICO. So a shelf listing (dataset, MCP tool, Apify actor) that hands out address-level rows to anyone is onward disclosure whose purpose we cannot police, with the owner as data controller of ~28M personal-data rows (ICO fee deferred, owner action 012) — the same category as the VOA list and Land Registry CCOD. A UPRN-only or aggregate product is OGL but still address-level personal data for the former and has no priced buyer for the latter. Demand and rivals: the official API is free, so a wrapper has no edge; Apify charles986/EpcIntelligenceActor resells it from $0.50 per 1,000 records and dhrumil/epc-scraper at $30/month + usage (scraping the register site); Searchland sells an EPC API inside its property licence on quote (28M+ certificates, monthly refresh, geocoded); no published per-lead price for ECO4 retrofit leads (renewables leads £7–£75 each per a 2026-09 survey of nine suppliers), and ECO4 itself ends 2026-12-31 with the Warm Homes Plan grant programme taking over in 2027 — the lead market this would sell into is sunsetting. Declined on licence and personal data, not on demand.
ideas.trigger: a buyer who is itself a permitted user under the OS/Royal Mail notice (a PAS 2030 installer, a letting agent, a council) asks for a private per-customer feed under their own purpose and controllership — then a bespoke delivery, never a shelf listing; or MHCLG publishes postcode-sector or LSOA aggregates under OGL and a paying user of the no-website or care-locations feeds asks for an energy-rating column

ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-13 (burn-down starvation fallback), read through the relay (docs/relay/responses/cro-ireland-{,2-}2026-10-13, pruned after 7 days) plus WebSearch. Supply: the Companies Registration Office opened opendata.cro.ie (CKAN, Derilinx) in 2024 — dataset 'companies': a daily snapshot of every Irish company incl. dissolved ones, 825,798 rows on 2026-10-13 (datastore_search total; metadata_modified 04:01 UTC that day), 21 fields (company_num, company_name, status + code, type + code, company_reg_date, last_ar_date, four address lines, comp_dissolved_date, nard = next annual return date, last_accounts_date, company_status_date, nace_v2_code, eircode, name/type effective dates, princ_object_code), a zipped CSV download and the keyless CKAN datastore API (/api/3/action/datastore_search?resource_id=3fef41bc-…, answered 200 to the relay; the zip answered 403 to a GitHub runner, so ingest would go through the API or needs a browser user agent). A second dataset 'financial' (filed financial statements) exists. No director, officer or business-name fields — those stay behind CRO Open Services (free REST API after a signed terms form, pay-per-document for account holders) and the licensed daily bulk feed (€31,000 p.a. per cro.ie's fee page, read second-hand: cro.ie answers 403 to the runner). Licence, verbatim from opendata.cro.ie/about and the package metadata: license_id CC-BY-4.0, high_value_dataset true (EU Implementing Regulation 2023/138, category 'Companies and company ownership'); 'Under the CC-BY Licence, users must acknowledge the source of the Information in their product or application … "Contains Irish Public Sector Data licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence"' — the cleanest licence of any register researched this month (no address-field carve-out, no purpose restriction). Personal data: company records only, registered-office addresses, no natural persons — Blind Mode has nothing to drop. Demand and rivals: CRIF owns both Irish incumbents — Vision-net's price list (vision-net.ie/prices.jsp) sells a Full Company Search at €2.10, Document View €5, Business Name Search €2.50 and an Annual Subscription at €300/yr, SoloCheck is 'FREE to start searching every Irish Company & their directors' and sells monitoring ('daily alerts'), credit reports and judgments — their paid value is directors, judgments and credit scores, none of which the open dataset carries. On Apify three actors already resell this exact portal: nerolabs/ireland-cro-monitor ('Lookup & Monitor: Filing Alerts', from $10/1,000 lookups, 'agent-ready: pay per event (x402 and MCP)', flags status changes, new filings and dissolutions — the gankdat shape to the letter, 2 total users, 1 monthly, 0 ratings, modified a month ago), parseforge/ireland-cro-companies-scraper ($19/1,000, 2 users, 0 monthly) and scrapers_lat/ireland-cro-companies-scraper ($12.75/1,000, 1 user, 0 monthly). So the shelf signal is the same as uk-company-lookup's: gankdat's own Companies House lookup has 6 calls and 1 Apify run in 30 days and 0 paid, and the closest clone of what we would build has 2 users. Build ≈ 1 day (CKAN datastore pager or zip ingest, D1 idOf on company_num, daily snapshot diff → change feed of incorporations, status changes and dissolutions, NACE and county filters, stats page, actor), £0, no account, the attribution line on every listing. Parked on demand, not licence: the one evidence that would move it is a paid call on any company-register endpoint, ours or a rival's. — Research 2026-10-19 (burn-down): the sibling EU one-feed idea is `spike-eu-hvd-company-registers` in new-ventures (member-state status count, OpenCorporates £2,250–12,000 a year for 500–5,000 calls a month as the rival price). — Spike 2026-10-19 (docs/exchange/spikes/eu-hvd-company-registers.md): the sibling EU feed is parked on the same evidence: seven member-state registers are keyless and open (IE, FR, FI, PL, LV, SE, MT) but DE, IT and ES publish none and NL strips the names, and on Apify the open registers' actors draw 1–4 users a month while the closed registers' scrapers draw 10–77; a Germany/Italy/Spain route by scraping is declined (their terms forbid it).

Unread: whether the vendor profile is self-serve or only after the 'book a call' on the provider page (an owner call would exceed the 15-minute cap; a form or an email would not), whether requests for UK registers appear at all (the browse page lists providers by use case), what Nomad asks of a UK individual (identity, company, data-licensing attestation) and how a request is answered (a form reply or a contract process the Worker cannot serve). Requests are private ('there are no listings'), the only trace of UK-register demand is seven SEO use-case pages (UK public sector contracts ×2, corporate and beneficial ownership, business compliance, UK business locations, US corporate registration), the visible provider library (30 cards) shows one emerging-markets sanctions/PEP vendor and two procurement-data vendors, no UK register vendor and no prices (vendors price off-platform), and the buyers pay US$300 per seat or US$1,000–3,000 a month to search for 'unique, niche, previously unattainable' data.
